why: The trace starts correctly, but the student says total is 'still 11.5, because it already has a value'. That is the static-variable misconception: in Java the assignment replaces the value, so the last line gives 11.5 + 11.5 × 0.08 = 12.42.

concepts.quote: after the last line total is still 11.5, because it already has a value
concepts.why: The student thinks a variable keeps its first value after a new assignment, but in Java each assignment replaces the old value, so total becomes 12.42.
The code has no loop or running total, so the answer says nothing about the accumulator pattern; the wrong claim about the update is levelled under variable.
The value 11.5 is correct, but it is given without any reasoning about int being widened to double, and the way's boundary says a bare output is not levelled.
